100	import { z } from "zod";
101	import type { ShipmentFacts } from "../reconcile/types";
102	
103	/** Data a broker has that no shipping document carries. Entered in the UI. */
104	export const BrokerInputs = z.object({
105	  filerCode: z.string().regex(/^[A-Z0-9]{3}$/).optional().or(z.literal("")),
106	  entryNumber: z.string().optional(),
107	  entryType: z.string().default("01"),
108	  importerNumber: z.string().optional().describe("IRS/EIN (NN-NNNNNNNXX) or CBP-assigned number"),
109	  bondType: z.enum(["", "continuous", "single"]).default(""),
110	  suretyCode: z.string().optional(),
111	  portOfEntry: z.string().optional(),
112	  estimatedArrival: z.string().optional(),
113	  referenceNumber: z.string().optional(),
114	  // Overrides for values the documents got wrong or left open
115	  importerOverride: z.enum(["", "buyer", "consignee"]).default(""),
116	  htsOverrides: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).default({}), // line key -> 10-digit HTS
117	  quantityOverrides: z.record(z.string(), z.number()).default({}),
118	});
119	export type BrokerInputs = z.infer<typeof BrokerInputs>;
120	
121	export interface MissingField {
122	  field: string;
123	  label: string;
124	  required: boolean;
125	  reason: string;
126	}
127	
128	/** Apply broker inputs on top of reconciled facts. Pure. */
129	export function applyBrokerInputs(facts: ShipmentFacts, b: BrokerInputs): ShipmentFacts {
130	  const f: ShipmentFacts = structuredClone(facts);
131	  f.entryType = b.entryType || f.entryType;
132	  if (b.portOfEntry) f.usPortCode = b.portOfEntry;
133	  if (b.estimatedArrival) f.arrivalDate = b.estimatedArrival;
134	  if (b.importerOverride === "consignee" && f.consignee) f.importer = f.consignee;
135	  if (b.importerOverride === "buyer" && f.buyer) f.importer = f.buyer;
136	  for (const l of f.lines) {
137	    const hts = b.htsOverrides[l.key]?.replace(/\D/g, "");
138	    if (hts && hts.length === 10) l.htsNumber = hts;
139	    const q = b.quantityOverrides[l.key];
140	    if (q !== undefined && l.unitPrice !== null && !l.noCommercialValue) {
141	      l.quantity = q;
142	      l.amountCents = Math.round(q * l.unitPrice * 100);
143	      l.enteredValueCents = l.amountCents + l.assistCents;
144	    } else if (q !== undefined) {
145	      l.quantity = q;
146	    }
147	  }
148	  if (f.lines.every((l) => l.enteredValueCents !== null)) f.enteredValueCents = f.lines.reduce((a, l) => a + l.enteredValueCents!, 0);
149	  return f;
150	}
151	
152	export function missingFields(f: ShipmentFacts, b: BrokerInputs): MissingField[] {
153	  const m: MissingField[] = [];
154	  const need = (cond: boolean, field: string, label: string, reason: string, required = true) => {
155	    if (cond) m.push({ field, label, required, reason });
156	  };
157	  need(!b.filerCode, "filerCode", "Broker filer code", "Assigned by CBP to the filing broker; never on shipping documents.");
158	  need(!b.entryNumber, "entryNumber", "Entry number", "NetCHB can assign the next number from the broker's range; leave blank to let it.", false);
159	  need(!b.importerNumber, "importerNumber", "Importer of record number (IRS/EIN)", `No document carries ${f.importer?.name ?? "the importer"}'s tax ID.`);
160	  need(!b.bondType, "bondType", "Bond type", "Continuous or single-transaction bond; comes from the importer's account.");
161	  need(!b.suretyCode, "suretyCode", "Surety code", "Identifies the bond's surety company.", b.bondType === "single");
162	  need(!f.usPortCode, "portOfEntry", "Port of entry", "Could not map the discharge port to a CBP Schedule D code.");
163	  need(!f.arrivalDate, "estimatedArrival", "Estimated arrival date", "Not found on the documents.");
164	  for (const l of f.lines) {
165	    need(!l.htsNumber, `hts.${l.key}`, `10-digit HTSUS for ${l.sku ?? l.key}`, `Documents give only ${l.hsAsPrinted ?? "no code"}.`);
166	  }
167	  for (const mf of f.manufacturers) need(!mf.mid, `mid.${mf.key}`, `MID for ${mf.name}`, mf.midNeedsReview.join("; "));
168	  return m;
169	}
170	=== src/lib/netchb/codes.ts
171	/**
172	 * Small lookup tables. Deliberately incomplete: an unknown value becomes a finding
173	 * for the broker, never a guess. Port codes are CBP Schedule D (district+port).
174	 */
175	const US_PORTS: Array<[RegExp, string, string]> = [
176	  [/\bTACOMA\b/i, "3002", "Tacoma, WA"],
177	  [/\bSEATTLE\b/i, "3001", "Seattle, WA"],
178	  [/\bLOS ANGELES\b/i, "2704", "Los Angeles, CA"],
179	  [/\bLONG BEACH\b/i, "2709", "Long Beach, CA"],
180	  [/\bOAKLAND\b/i, "2811", "Oakland, CA"],
181	  [/\bNEW YORK\b|\bNEWARK\b|\bELIZABETH\b/i, "4601", "New York/Newark"],
182	  [/\bSAVANNAH\b/i, "1703", "Savannah, GA"],
183	  [/\bCHARLESTON\b/i, "1601", "Charleston, SC"],
184	  [/\bNORFOLK\b/i, "1401", "Norfolk, VA"],
185	  [/\bHOUSTON\b/i, "5301", "Houston, TX"],
186	  [/\bMIAMI\b/i, "5201", "Miami, FL"],
187	  [/\bBALTIMORE\b/i, "1303", "Baltimore, MD"],
188	  [/\bCHICAGO\b/i, "3901", "Chicago, IL"],
189	  [/\bJFK\b|KENNEDY/i, "4701", "JFK Airport, NY"],
190	];
191	
192	export function usPortCode(text: string | null): { code: string; name: string } | null {
193	  if (!text) return null;
194	  for (const [re, code, name] of US_PORTS) if (re.test(text)) return { code, name };
195	  return null;

208	=== src/app/api/extract/route.ts
209	import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
210	import { ExtractionError, extractFile } from "@/lib/extract/client";
211	
212	export const runtime = "nodejs";
213	export const maxDuration = 120;
214	
215	const MAX_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024;
216	
217	/** multipart files → DocumentExtraction[]. The only route that calls the model. */
218	export async function POST(req: Request) {
219	  if (!process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) {
220	    return NextResponse.json({ error: "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set on the server." }, { status: 500 });
221	  }
222	  const form = await req.formData();
223	  const files = form.getAll("files").filter((f): f is File => f instanceof File);
224	  if (!files.length) return NextResponse.json({ error: "No files uploaded." }, { status: 400 });
225	
226	  const results = await Promise.allSettled(
227	    files.map(async (f) => {
228	      if (f.size > MAX_BYTES) throw new ExtractionError("File is larger than 20 MB", f.name);
229	      const base64 = Buffer.from(await f.arrayBuffer()).toString("base64");
230	      const mediaType = f.type || (f.name.toLowerCase().endsWith(".pdf") ? "application/pdf" : "application/octet-stream");
231	      return extractFile({ name: f.name, mediaType, base64 });
232	    }),
233	  );
234	
235	  const documents = results.flatMap((r) => (r.status === "fulfilled" ? r.value : []));
236	  const errors = results.flatMap((r, i) =>
237	    r.status === "rejected" ? [{ file: files[i].name, error: r.reason instanceof Error ? r.reason.message : String(r.reason) }] : [],
238	  );
239	  return NextResponse.json({ documents, errors });
240	}

523	=== scripts/eval-extraction.ts
524	/**
525	 * Extraction accuracy check: runs the real model on the sample PDFs and compares the
526	 * output field-by-field with the hand-transcribed fixture. Then runs reconciliation on
527	 * the MODEL's output to confirm every known trap is still caught end to end.
528	 *
529	 *   ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... npx tsx scripts/eval-extraction.ts
530	 */
531	import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
532	import { join } from "node:path";
533	import { extractFile } from "../src/lib/extract/client";
534	import type { ExtractedDoc } from "../src/lib/extract/schema";
535	import { reconcile } from "../src/lib/reconcile";
536	import { shipment001 } from "../fixtures/shipment-001/extraction";
537	
538	const DIR = join(__dirname, "../fixtures/shipment-001");
539	const norm = (v: unknown) => (typeof v === "string" ? v.toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9.%/]/g, "") : JSON.stringify(v));
540	
541	// The fields that matter downstream. Free text (notes, descriptions) is checked for presence, not wording.
542	const SCALARS = ["docType", "documentNumber", "documentDateRaw", "currency", "incoterm", "houseBill", "masterBill"] as const;
543	const LINE_FIELDS = ["styleOrSku", "hsCode", "quantity", "unitPrice", "amount", "excludedFromTotal", "cartons", "piecesPerCarton", "grossWeightKg", "netWeightKg"] as const;
544	const TOTALS = ["subtotal", "grandTotal", "totalQuantity", "totalPackages", "grossWeightKg", "netWeightKg"] as const;
545	
546	let ok = 0, total = 0;
547	const misses: string[] = [];
548	const check = (label: string, got: unknown, want: unknown) => {
549	  if (want === null || want === undefined) return; // only score fields that exist on the page
550	  total++;
551	  if (norm(got) === norm(want)) ok++;
552	  else misses.push(`${label}: got ${JSON.stringify(got)}, want ${JSON.stringify(want)}`);
553	};
554	
555	async function main() {
556	  const extracted: ExtractedDoc[] = [];
557	  for (const want of shipment001) {
558	    const base64 = readFileSync(join(DIR, want.sourceFile)).toString("base64");
559	    const t0 = Date.now();
560	    const docs = await extractFile({ name: want.sourceFile, mediaType: "application/pdf", base64 });
561	    console.log(`${want.sourceFile}: ${docs.length} document(s) in ${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1)}s`);
562	    extracted.push(...docs);
563	    const got = docs.find((d) => d.docType === want.docType) ?? docs[0];
564	    for (const f of SCALARS) check(`${want.docType}.${f}`, got[f], want[f]);
565	    for (const f of TOTALS) check(`${want.docType}.totals.${f}`, got.totals[f], want.totals[f]);
566	    want.lineItems.forEach((wl, i) => {
567	      const gl = got.lineItems.find((x) => norm(x.styleOrSku) === norm(wl.styleOrSku)) ?? got.lineItems[i];
568	      for (const f of LINE_FIELDS) check(`${want.docType}.line${i + 1}.${f}`, gl?.[f], wl[f]);
569	    });
570	    check(`${want.docType}.amendments`, got.amendments.length, want.amendments.length);
571	    check(`${want.docType}.manufacturers`, got.parties.filter((p) => p.role === "manufacturer").length, want.parties.filter((p) => p.role === "manufacturer").length || null);
572	  }
573	
574	  console.log(`\nField accuracy: ${ok}/${total} (${((ok / total) * 100).toFixed(1)}%)`);
575	  misses.forEach((m) => console.log("  MISS " + m));
576	
577	  const r = reconcile(extracted);
578	  const ids = new Set(r.findings.map((f) => f.id));
579	  const traps = ["LINE_EXTENSION_MISMATCH", "QUANTITY_MISMATCH", "ASSIST_DETECTED", "LINE_ORIGIN_DIFFERS", "IMPORTER_OF_RECORD",
580	    "SELLER_NOT_MANUFACTURER", "DOCUMENT_AMENDED", "GROSS_WEIGHT_MISMATCH", "FIBRE_MISMATCH", "DATE_AMBIGUOUS", "MARKING_ORIGIN_CONFLICT"];
581	  console.log(`\nEnd-to-end traps caught from model output: ${traps.filter((t) => ids.has(t)).length}/${traps.length}`);
582	  traps.filter((t) => !ids.has(t)).forEach((t) => console.log("  MISSED " + t));
583	  console.log(`Entered value: ${(r.facts.enteredValueCents ?? 0) / 100} (fixture: 27439)`);
584	}
585	
586	main().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });

Port code 3002 is Tacoma, Washington, in CBP's Schedule D system of domestic port codes. Each code has four digits, where the first two identify the customs district and the last two identify the port within it. Schedule D port codes are the official numeric identifiers that U.S. Customs and Border Protection assigns to every domestic port of entry.

Here is what the results show about 3002:

- **Location and hours:** One CBP port information page lists code 3002 at 2202 Port of Tacoma Road, Tacoma, WA 98421, with a general phone of (253) 593-6336. It gives weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Pacific. That page appears to be an older archived record, so confirm the details before relying on them.
- **Oversight:** An FDA page lists 3002 (Tacoma, WA) among the port codes covered by the Tacoma Resident Post, at 949 Market Street, Tacoma. The same list includes 3029 (Sea-Tac Airport) and 3003 (Aberdeen–Hoquiam).
- **Operational status:** A 2015 CBP bulletin says that Seattle seaport 3001, Tacoma 3002, and Sea-Tac air cargo 3029 were the main codes affected by a change in cargo release processing for the Seattle area. A 2014 bulletin said the Port of Tacoma (3002) remained fully operational during a Seattle-specific grace period.

One source to disregard: a calcmytariff.com page says the combined Seattle/Tacoma Northwest Seaport Alliance uses code 3001 for both ports. Its content looks unreliable, and it cites a CSMS number that I could not verify. The CBP sources above treat 3001 as Seattle and 3002 as Tacoma as separate ports, so I would not rely on that page.

For a current and authoritative answer, check CBP's official Schedule D list, which is the source the commercial directories draw from. If you're filing an entry, confirm the code with your customs broker or with the CBP Tacoma office.

The search turned up mostly secondary sources and a few SDK docs. I didn't find the official REST reference for `responseJsonSchema` or an official inline-PDF example, so verify the field names against the current API reference before relying on them.

**Schema field: `responseJsonSchema` vs. `responseSchema`**
- Gemini 2.5 and later accept a full JSON Schema through `generationConfig.responseJsonSchema`. It is mutually exclusive with responseSchema and requires responseMimeType, so set `responseMimeType` to `application/json` alongside it and don't send both schema fields.
- The older `responseSchema` field accepts only a subset of the OpenAPI 3.0 spec rather than JSON Schema. That subset does not cover unions or records, which is the main reason to switch to `responseJsonSchema`.

**Inline PDF**
- One third-party guide says the second, more performant path for single-page or small PDFs is to base64-encode the file bytes and pass them directly in the contents array as an inline_data part with mime_type application/pdf. That guide is a Python SDK walkthrough, so in REST the equivalent JSON keys are camelCase (`inlineData`, `mimeType`, `data`).
- The same guide notes that uploading to the Gemini File API and referencing its URI works well for documents over a few pages.

**Putting it together (REST shape, from my own knowledge rather than the sources)**

```
POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent
x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY

{
  "contents": [{
    "parts": [
      { "inlineData": { "mimeType": "application/pdf", "data": "<base64 PDF bytes>" } },
      { "text": "Extract the invoice fields." }
    ]
  }],
  "generationConfig": {
    "responseMimeType": "application/json",
    "responseJsonSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { ... }, "required": [ ... ] }
  }
}
```

Keep the inline request body small: base64 inflates the payload by about a third, so large PDFs should go through the File API.

**JSON Schema keywords:**

- **Types:** `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `object`, `array`, `null`.
- **Nullable:** Use a type array, such as `{"type": ["string", "null"]}`.
- **Object:** `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties`.
- **String:** `enum`, `format` (`date-time`, `date`, `time`).
- **Number/integer:** `enum`, `minimum`, `maximum`.
- **Array:** `items`, `prefixItems`, `minItems`, `maxItems`.
- **Annotations:** `title`, `description`.
- **`anyOf`:** Not in the supported lists, but the Content Moderation example uses it. The page doesn't document it explicitly.
- **`$ref`:** The recursive example uses `"$ref": "#"` for self-reference. The page doesn't list it as supported.
- **Limits:** Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported, and very large or deeply nested schemas may be rejected.

**Models in examples:** Most examples use `gemini-3.8-flash`. The structured outputs with tools example uses `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`.

Upload PDF or image files.`, file.name);\n  }\n  let feedback: string | null = null;\n  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) {\n    const { output, truncated } = await provider.transcribe(file, feedback);\n    const parsed = FileExtraction.safeParse(output);\n    if (parsed.success) return parsed.data.documents.map((d) => ({ ...d, sourceFile: file.name }));\n    if (truncated) throw new ExtractionError(\"Document too long to transcribe in one pass\", file.name);\n    feedback = output === null ? \"Your reply was not valid JSON.\" : z.prettifyError(parsed.error);\n    if (attempt === 1) throw new ExtractionError(`Extraction by ${provider.name} did not match the schema after a retry`, file.name, parsed.error.issues);\n  }\n  throw new ExtractionError(\"unreachable\", file.name);\n}\n"
}

All arithmetic, valuation, origin, party roles and MID construction are TypeScript that can be read and tested. Money is integer cents.\n- **Nothing changes silently.** A rule that changes a value emits a finding with `autoApplied: true`, the before and after values, the evidence quoted from the documents, and what the broker must still do.\n- **Edits are free.** Correcting a misread number, entering an HTS code or picking the importer of record rebuilds findings and XML through `/api/entry` with no model call.\n\n```\nsrc/lib/extract/        prompt, Zod schema, Gemini + Anthropic providers, retry loop\nsrc/lib/reconcile/      facts.ts (who supplies which field), rules/ (one file per rule), mid.ts\nsrc/lib/netchb/         map.ts (facts → XSD tree), build.ts, validate.ts, codes.ts, brokerInputs.ts\nsrc/lib/pipeline.ts     reconcile → broker inputs → map → XML → validate\nschemas/                NetCHB entry.xsd + data_type.xsd, and SOURCE.md: how they were found\nfixtures/shipment-001/  sample PDFs + hand-written expected extraction (not model-generated)\n```\n\nAdding a rule means one file in `src/lib/reconcile/rules/`, one line in `src/lib/reconcile/index.ts`, and one test.\n\n## How NetCHB was tracked down\n\nThe brief gave no link. The full trail, with dead ends, is in [`schemas/SOURCE.md`](schemas/SOURCE.md). In short:\n\n1. NetCHB's JBossWS service index at `www.netchb.com/main/services/...` exposed the `EntryUploadService` WSDL: `uploadEntry(username, password, entryXml)`, RPC/literal. The WSDL types the entry as a plain string, so its structure lives elsewhere.\n2. Guessed paths under `/xml/` found `https://www.netchb.com/xml/entry/entry.xsd`. Its import pointed to `https://www.netchb.com/xml/data/data_type.xsd`. Both are committed untouched (plus a working copy with the import repointed locally), with SHA-256 hashes.\n3. The schema's own annotations then confirmed what had been assumptions: `<transmit/>` is what sends to CBP, and NetCHB computes duty unless `<precalculated/>` is present.\n\n## Safety: this never files anything\n\n- The XML has **no `<transmit/>` tag**. Per `entry.xsd`, uploading it to NetCHB stages the entry for a licensed broker to review and transmit.\n- The app has **no NetCHB credentials** and makes no SOAP call.\n- It **never computes duty**. NetCHB does that from the tariff numbers.\n\n## What it does not do (and says so)\n\n- **No 10-digit HTS classification.** Invoices carry 6-digit HS. The XML carries the digits exactly as printed (schema-valid, never zero-padded to look real), and every line is flagged for the broker. Reporting units (e.g. DOZ + KG for apparel) follow from the 10-digit number.\n- **No Chapter 99 / Section 301 / AD-CVD / PGA handling.** Origin is set per line so NetCHB's own remedy logic can work, but the app does not stack trade remedies.\n- **The MID is built from CBP's published rules, not looked up.** Ambiguous addresses (e.g. \"Lot C7-C8\") are flagged for checking against the broker's NetCHB manufacturer table.\n- **The importer of record is proposed, never decided silently.** The buyer is preferred over a 3PL consignee, and the choice is flagged and switchable.\n- **One `<invoice>` per entry.** With several invoices, lines are merged and a warning says so.\n- **Untested against a live NetCHB account.** Passing the XSD is necessary, not sufficient: NetCHB and CBP enforce business rules the schema does not express.\n- **Small code tables.** Port codes, countries and package units cover common cases. Anything unknown becomes a finding, not a guess. Schedule K foreign port codes are not mapped.\n"

11	/** Overload and rate-limit errors are transient: retry them with backoff. Anything else fails at once. */
12	const TRANSIENT = new Set([429, 500, 502, 503, 504]);
13	const BACKOFF_MS = [2_000, 5_000, 10_000];
14	
15	async function fetchWithRetry(url: string, init: RequestInit): Promise<Response> {
16	  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
17	    const res = await fetch(url, init);
18	    if (!TRANSIENT.has(res.status) || attempt >= BACKOFF_MS.length) return res;
19	    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, BACKOFF_MS[attempt]));

23	/**
24	 * Gemini over plain REST (no SDK dependency). PDFs and images go inline; the response is
25	 * constrained to our JSON Schema with responseMimeType + responseJsonSchema.
26	 */
27	export function geminiProvider(jsonSchema: object, model = process.env.GEMINI_MODEL ?? "gemini-3.8-flash"): ExtractionProvider {
28	  const key = process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY ?? "";
29	  return {
30	    name: `gemini:${model}`,
31	    async transcribe(file, retryFeedback) {
32	      const res = await fetchWithRetry(`${ENDPOINT}/${encodeURIComponent(model)}:generateContent`, {
33	        method: "POST",
34	        headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-goog-api-key": key },
35	        body: JSON.stringify({
36	          systemInstruction: { parts: [{ text: EXTRACTION_SYSTEM }] },
37	          contents: [{
38	            role: "user",
39	            parts: [
40	              { inlineData: { mimeType: file.mediaType, data: file.base64 } },
41	              { text: retryFeedback ? `${EXTRACTION_USER}\n\n${retryText(retryFeedback)}` : EXTRACTION_USER },
42	            ],
43	          }],
44	          generationConfig: { temperature: 0, maxOutputTokens: 32768, responseMimeType: "application/json", responseJsonSchema: jsonSchema },
45	        }),
46	      });
47	      const body = (await res.json()) as GeminiResponse;
48	      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Gemini API ${res.status}: ${body.error?.message ?? "request failed"}`);
49	      const cand = body.candidates?.[0];
50	      const text = cand?.content?.parts?.map((p) => p.text ?? "").join("") ?? "";
51	      let output: unknown = null;
52	      try {
53	        output = JSON.parse(text);
54	      } catch {
55	        output = null; // reported as a schema failure and retried
56	      }
57	      return { output, truncated: cand?.finishReason === "MAX_TOKENS" };
58	    },

function collectManufacturers(docs: ExtractedDoc[], seller: PartyFact | null): ManufacturerFact[] {
  const out: ManufacturerFact[] = [];
  const add = (p: PartyFact) => {
    const existing = out.find((m) => sameCompany(m.name, p.name));
    if (existing) {
      existing.sources = [...new Set([...existing.sources, ...p.sources])];
      return;
    }
    const mid = buildMid({ name: p.name, streetLine: p.addressLines[0] ?? null, city: p.city, countryIso: p.countryIso, province: p.state });
    out.push({ ...p, key: `M${out.length + 1}`, mid: mid.mid, midNeedsReview: mid.needsReview });
  };
  for (const d of docs) for (const p of d.parties) if (p.role === "manufacturer") add(toPartyFact(p, d.docType));
  // A transport-doc shipper that is not the seller is very often the factory.
  if (out.length === 0) {
    for (const d of docsOf(docs, "bill_of_lading", "air_waybill", "packing_list"))
      for (const p of d.parties)
        if (p.role === "shipper" && (!seller || !sameCompany(p.name, seller.name))) add(toPartyFact(p, d.docType));
  }
  // Nobody else is named: the seller is very often the factory itself. Assume it, and say so.
  if (out.length === 0 && seller && seller.countryIso && seller.countryIso !== "US") {
    add(seller);
    out[0].assumedFromSeller = true;
  }
  return out;
}

17	 * What the model read, exactly as printed. Fix a misread here and everything downstream

20	export function DocumentsPanel({ docs, onChange }: Props) {

Arrays compare by index. */\nexport function diffJson(a: unknown, b: unknown, path = \"\"): ManualEdit[] {\n  if (Object.is(a, b)) return [];\n  const isObj = (v: unknown): v is Record<string, unknown> => typeof v === \"object\" && v !== null;\n  if (isObj(a) && isObj(b) && Array.isArray(a) === Array.isArray(b)) {\n    const keys = [...new Set([...Object.keys(a), ...Object.keys(b)])];\n    return keys.flatMap((k) => diffJson(a[k], b[k], Array.isArray(a) ? `${path}[${k}]` : path ? `${path}.${k}` : k));\n  }\n  return [{ path, extracted: a ?? null, reviewed: b ?? null }];\n}\n\n/** A file-name-safe reference for the entry: the entry number if the broker gave one. */\nexport function entryReference(facts: ShipmentFacts, broker: BrokerInputs): string {\n  if (broker.filerCode && broker.entryNumber) return `${broker.filerCode}-${broker.entryNumber}`.toUpperCase();\n  return (facts.houseBill ?? facts.masterBill ?? facts.invoiceNumber ?? \"draft\").replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9-]/g, \"\");\n}\n\nexport interface AuditInput {\n  extractedByModel: ExtractedDoc[];\n  reviewed: ExtractedDoc[];\n  broker: BrokerInputs;\n  result: EntryResult;\n  generatedAt: string;\n  sha256: Record<string, string>; // file name (or \"entry.xml\") → hex digest\n}\n\nexport function buildAuditRecord({ extractedByModel, reviewed, broker, result, generatedAt, sha256 }: AuditInput): AuditRecord {\n  const files = [...new Set(extractedByModel.map((d) => d.sourceFile))];\n  const notFiling = (f: Finding) => f.category !== \"filing\";\n  return {\n    format: \"sefer-entry-prep/audit-trail@1\",\n    generatedAt,\n    recordkeeping:\n      \"Supporting record for 19 CFR Part 163. **What was added:**

## Improvements found (nothing changed yet; your call)

**Correctness:**
- **#2 Two invoices: false errors.** Two invoices that are each internally correct get flagged as subtotal and total *errors*, because all lines are checked against the first invoice's totals.
- **#5 Misread bill number.** In the combined-PDF run the model read the master bill as `SGN26091775` instead of `SGN260917735`. Nothing in the documents can catch it by cross-checking. Possible fix: read critical identifiers (bill and container numbers) twice and flag any disagreement. That adds one extra model call per upload.
- **#3 Raw validator messages.** Missing data shows libxml text instead of plain advice like "Line 1 has no tariff number; enter the 10-digit HTS".

**Robustness and UX:**
- **#4 Files over 4.5 MB** show a cryptic JSON error. Fix: check size before uploading and say why.
- **#1 Malformed API requests** return 500 instead of 400. This doesn't affect the UI.
- **#6 Mobile:** the PDF pane pushes the findings down, and phones often can't display PDFs inline. Fix: on phones, show "Open document" buttons instead.
- **#7 Open extraction endpoint:** anyone with the URL can spend your Gemini quota. Easiest fix: set a usage cap in Google AI Studio (no code). Alternatively, a simple passcode.

**Please check one thing yourself:** open the URL in desktop Chrome or Edge and confirm the PDF shows in the left pane. My headless browser can't display PDFs.

async function extract() {
    setBusy("extract");
    setErrors([]);
    try {
      const form = new FormData();
      files.forEach((f) => form.append("files", f));
      const res = await fetch("/api/extract", { method: "POST", body: form });
      const body = await res.json();
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(body.error ?? res.statusText);
      setErrors((body.errors ?? []).map((e: { file: string; error: string }) => `${e.file}: ${e.error}`));
      if (body.documents?.length) {

      }
    } catch (e) {
      setErrors([e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)]);

===== ASSISTANT [2026-10-09 16:31:53] =====
**Short answer:** Groq's daily request count is much higher on paper, but for this app switching would *lower* real capacity, and it would cost real engineering work and accuracy risk. More detail below.

## Gemini (your current key, free tier)

| What | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Requests per day, per model | **20** | The 429 error your key returned today: `quotaValue: "20"` for both `gemini-3.8-flash` and `gemini-3.5-flash` |
| Applies to | The whole **Google project**, not each key | Google's rate-limits page |
| Resets | Midnight Pacific time | Google's rate-limits page |
| Your app's total | About **100 requests/day**, because each of the 5 models in the chain has its own 20 | The model list I set up |

Each uploaded file is one request (the second read is off), so 100 requests is roughly **30 three-document shipments a day**, when the models aren't overloaded. Google no longer publishes exact per-model numbers; your real limits are at **aistudio.google.com/rate-limit**. A new key in the same project shares the same quota.

## Groq: why it's worse here

| | Gemini free | Groq `qwen/qwen3.8-27b` (its only vision model) |
|---|---|---|
| Requests per day | 20 per model | 1,000 *(Developer-plan table; free plan unconfirmed)* |
| **Tokens per minute** | high | **8,000** |
| **Tokens per day** | high | **200,000** |
| Reads PDFs directly | ✅ | ❌ images only, max 3 per request |

**Tokens are the real limit, not requests.** Groq counts each page image as about 2,048 input tokens, and our structured answer adds a few thousand more. That's an estimated 5–8K tokens per page, against these limits:
- **8K tokens per minute** means about 1 page per minute, so the 4-page sample would take about 4 minutes or hit rate-limit errors.
- **200K tokens per day** means roughly 25–40 pages a day, *fewer* shipments than Gemini's chain gives.

**It would also cost real work and risk:**
- PDFs would have to be converted to images first. That means new rendering libraries, which are awkward on Vercel and conflict with your "few dependencies" rule.
- Pages would have to be split into requests of at most 3 images.
- A 27B open model is unproven on these scans. The handwritten container number and stamped-over text are exactly where small models struggle, and extraction accuracy is graded. `scripts/eval-extraction.ts` could measure it, but that would be speculative work right before submission.

## Recommendation

1. **Best: enable billing on the Google AI project with a budget cap** (for example a few dollars). Limits jump far above 20 a day, paid requests get priority when Gemini is busy (which fixes today's slowness), and a 3-document shipment costs well under a cent. No code changes.
2. **Without billing**, stay as you are: about 100 requests a day across the 5-model chain, a clear message when quota runs out, and the sample shipment always working. That's likely enough for graders, unless they upload heavily on the same day.
3. **Don't switch to Groq.**

I'd also avoid creating extra Google projects to get more free quota; that's the kind of limit-dodging the terms prohibit.

Sources:
- [Gemini API rate limits](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits)
- [Groq rate limits](https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits)
- [Groq vision docs](https://console.groq.com/docs/vision)

[Glossary](#9-glossary)\n10. [Limits and further reading](#10-limits-and-further-reading)\n\n---\n\n## 1. About this manual\n\nThis manual shows how to turn a shipment's documents into a NetCHB entry file with the Sefer Entry Prep website. It covers every screen, each task step by step, and what to do when something goes wrong.\n\n**Conventions**\n\n- **Bold text** is a label or button on screen, for example **Use sample shipment**.\n- The numbered blue badges in each screenshot match the numbered steps beside it.\n- ⚠️ marks something that affects what is filed with U.S. Customs.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Product overview\n\n### What it does\n\nYou upload a shipment's documents: the commercial invoice, the packing list, and the bill of lading or air waybill, as PDFs or photos. The website:\n\n1. **Reads the documents.** An AI model transcribes what each page says, including errors, crossed-out values and footnotes.\n2. **Checks them against each other.** Rules written in code recompute every number, compare the documents line by line, and apply customs valuation (for example, removing freight from a CIF price or adding a buyer-supplied material as an assist).\n3. **Lists its findings.** Every discrepancy, every value it changed (with the before and after values and the reason), and every field no document can supply.\n4. **Produces the NetCHB entry file.** It builds a Type 01 consumption entry in NetCHB's XML format and checks it against NetCHB's published schema.\n\n### What it does not do\n\n- ⚠️ **It never files anything.** The XML has no transmit instruction, so uploading it to NetCHB only stages the entry. A licensed broker reviews it in NetCHB and transmits it from there.\n- **It does not classify goods to 10-digit HTS numbers.** Invoices usually give 6 digits; the broker enters the full number.\n- **It does not calculate duty.** NetCHB does that from the tariff numbers.\n- **It never silently picks between conflicting values.** When two readings disagree, it shows both and asks you.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Getting started\n\n### What you need\n\n| Item | Details |\n|---|---|\n| A web browser | A current version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. A desktop screen is recommended; phones are supported for review. |\n| Documents | PDF, PNG, JPG or WEBP. Scans and phone photos are fine. |\n| File size | Up to **4.4 MB per file** on the website. |\n| An access code | Only if your administrator has switched one on. The sample shipment never needs one. |\n\n### Quick start (5 minutes)\n\n1. Open **https://sefer-webapp.vercel.app**.\n2. Click **Use sample shipment** to load a real example, or choose your own files and click **Extract**.\n3. Work through the **Findings**, starting with the red errors.\n4. Fill in the **Broker inputs** and the 10-digit **HTS** numbers.\n5. When the XML panel shows **Valid against NetCHB entry.xsd**, click **Download**.\n\n---\n\n## 4. A tour of the screen\n\n![Main screen after loading a shipment](manual/images/02-overview.png)\n\n1. **Progress bar.** It shows where you are: **Documents → Findings → Broker → XML**. A green ✓ means done; an amber **!** means something needs your attention. Click any step to jump to it. It stays at the top of the screen as you scroll.\n2. **Source documents.** The original document, always beside your work, so you can check any value against the page.\n3. **The review area**, in numbered sections:\n\n| Section | What it is for |\n|---|---|\n| ① **Shipment documents** | Upload files or load the sample. |\n| ② **Findings** | Every discrepancy, correction and open question, with evidence. |\n| ③ **Broker inputs** | Information only the broker has (importer number, bond, entry date…). |\n| ④ **Entry lines** | Each line as it will be entered: value, origin, manufacturer ID, HTS. |\n| ⑤ **NetCHB entry XML** | The file for NetCHB, its validation result, copy and download. |\n| ⑥ **Compliance audit trail** | A record of how the entry was prepared, for your files. |\n| **Extracted documents** | Exactly what was read from each page, editable. |\n\nEvery change you make anywhere is applied in under a second. The findings and XML rebuild automatically; nothing is sent to the AI model again.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Step-by-step tasks\n\n### 5.1 Load your documents\n\n![Uploading documents](manual/images/01-home.png)\n\n1. Click the **drop zone** and choose your files. Select all of a shipment's documents at once, in any order. A single PDF that contains several documents also works.\n2. Click **Extract**. Each file is read separately; with several files the button shows **Reading 2 of 3…**. Scans can take from a few seconds to a couple of minutes.\n3. Or click **Use sample shipment** to load a real example instantly.\n\nWhen reading finishes, chips under the drop zone confirm what was recognised, for example 📄 **Invoice**, 📦 **Packing list**, 🚢 **Bill of lading**, each with its document number.\n\n> **Tip.** If a document type is missing from the chips, the file may not have been readable. Check the messages under the drop zone (see [Troubleshooting](#7-troubleshooting)).\n\n### 5.2 Check the source documents side by side\n\n![Source document viewer](manual/images/03-viewer.png)\n\n1. Use the **tabs** to switch between the invoice, packing list and bill of lading.\n2. Click **Open ↗** to open the document full size in a new browser tab.\n\nYou can also jump straight to the right document from a finding (step 5.3) or from **Extracted documents** (step 5.6).\n\n### 5.3 Work through the findings\n\n![Findings panel with one finding expanded](manual/images/04-findings.png)\n\n1. **Filter by severity.** The four counters show **Errors**, **Warnings**, **Info** and **XML notes**. Click a counter to show or hide that group. XML notes are hidden at first.\n2. **Open a finding** by clicking its title. You will see:\n   - what was found and why it matters;\n   - the **evidence**: short quotes from the documents, each labelled with its source;\n   - **What we did** (if the website changed a value) or **Action** (if you need to act).\n   - The green **auto-applied** badge means the website changed a value on the entry. The finding always shows both values and the reason.\n3. Click **view ↗** next to any quote to open that document in the viewer and check it yourself.\n\n**Recommended order:** errors first, then warnings, then info.\n\n### 5.4 Complete the broker inputs\n\n![Broker inputs form](manual/images/05-broker.png)\n\n1. The badge in the corner counts **required** items still open. It turns green (**✓ complete**) when everything required is filled in.\n2. Fill in the four groups:\n   - **Filing info:** filer code and entry number (leave blank to let NetCHB number the entry), entry date, your reference.\n   - **Parties:** importer of record (the website proposes one and explains why in the findings; change it here if needed), importer IRS/EIN number, ultimate consignee tax ID, related-party declaration.\n   - **Bond:** continuous (08) or single transaction (09), and surety code.\n   - **Transport:** port of entry (pre-filled when it can be derived) and container numbers (to override what was read).\n3. **No document can supply these** lists every remaining gap, marked **required** or **optional**, with the reason.\n\n### 5.5 Review the entry lines and enter HTS numbers\n\n![Entry lines table](manual/images/06-entry-lines.png)\n\n1. Type the **10-digit HTS number** for each line. The number printed on the invoice is shown underneath for reference. The website never pads a 6-digit code with zeros, because that would look like a real classification.\n2. Compare **Printed** with **Entered value**. A green highlight means the entered value differs from the printed one: a corrected arithmetic error (**corrected**), or an added assist (**incl. assist**). Free-of-charge lines carry a purple **FOC** badge and are still entered at their stated value.\n3. Check **Origin** and **MID** (manufacturer ID). A red origin badge means the line's own remarks give a different country from the rest of the shipment. **check** under a MID means it was built from an address CBP's rules don't settle cleanly; confirm it against your NetCHB manufacturer records.\n\nYou can also override a line's quantity in the **Qty** field.\n\n### 5.6 Correct a misread value\n\n![Extracted documents, editable](manual/images/09-documents.png)\n\n1. Under **Extracted documents**, open a document and click **View source** to show it in the viewer.\n2. Compare the values, and correct any misread **HS**, **Qty**, **Unit price** or **Amount** directly in the table.\n\nThe findings, values and XML update immediately. ⚠️ Edit only values that were *read* wrongly. If the document itself is wrong (for example, a typo on the invoice), leave it: the findings will flag it and the audit trail will record it.\n\n### 5.7 Resolve XML validation issues\n\n![Plain-language list of what to fix](manual/images/10-fix-it.png)\n\nWhen the XML does not yet meet NetCHB's schema, the panel shows a red **✗** and a list headed **What to fix before this can be uploaded to NetCHB**.\n\n1. Each item says what is missing and where to fix it, for example *\"Line NB-T101: no tariff number. Enter its 10-digit HTS under Entry lines.\"* Fix the items one by one; the list shrinks as you go.\n\nClick **Validator output** to see the schema validator's original messages, if you need them.\n\n### 5.8 Copy or download the NetCHB XML\n\n![NetCHB XML panel](manual/images/07-xml.png)\n\n1. Wait for the green **Valid against NetCHB entry.xsd** banner.\n2. Click **Copy** to put the XML on your clipboard, or **Download** to save it as a file (named after the bill of lading).\n\nThen upload the file to NetCHB through your account's XML upload or NetCHB's entry upload web service. ⚠️ The entry arrives **staged, not transmitted**. Review it in NetCHB, then transmit it from there.\n\n### 5.9 Export the compliance audit trail\n\n![Compliance audit trail](manual/images/08-audit.png)\n\n1. Click **Export compliance audit** to download `audit-trail-<entry>.json`.\n\nThe file records:\n- what the AI model read from each document;\n- every manual edit, with the value before and after;\n- each correction the rules made, with its evidence, kept separate from the issues still open;\n- your broker inputs;\n- the final XML and its validation result;\n- SHA-256 fingerprints of the source files, the XML and the schema, which tie the record to the exact documents used.\n\nThe three counters above the button summarise **Corrections applied**, **Open issues** and **Manual edits**. Keep the file with the shipment's commercial documents: entry records must be kept for five years from the date of entry (19 CFR 163.4). The audit file supports that record; it does not replace it.\n\n### 5.10 Use the website on a phone\n\n![Phone layout](manual/images/13-phone.png)\n\nOn a phone, the sections stack vertically. Instead of a document pane, **Source documents** shows a button for each document; tap one to open it in your phone's viewer. Uploading and reviewing work the same as on a desktop.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Reference\n\n### 6.1 Badges and colours\n\n| Badge | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| 🔴 **error** | Must be resolved before filing (a wrong value, a missing required item, or two documents that disagree). |\n| 🟠 **warning** | Needs a broker's judgement or confirmation. |\n| 🔵 **info** | Explains something the website did or assumed. |\n| 🟣 **xml** | How a value was fitted into NetCHB's format (for example, removing `/` from an invoice number). |\n| 🟢 **auto-applied** | The website changed a value on the entry; the finding shows both values. |\n| **FOC** / **assist** | Free-of-charge line / line whose value includes a buyer-supplied assist. |\n\n### 6.2 Common findings and what to do\n\n| Finding | What it means | What to do |\n|---|---|---|\n| Printed amount does not equal quantity × unit price | A line's arithmetic is wrong. If the invoice subtotal proves which figure is right, the website uses it. | Ask the seller for a corrected invoice. |\n| Invoice says X, packing list says Y | The two documents disagree on a style's quantity, even if their totals match. | Confirm the shipped count with the shipper. |\n| Buyer-supplied material is an assist | The price excludes materials the buyer provided; their value is added to the dutiable value. | Confirm the assist value with the importer. |\n| Line is made in a different country | A line's own remarks give a different origin from the rest of the shipment. | Confirm origin; check the carton marking. |\n| Importer of record assumed to be the buyer | The bill of lading consignee looks like a warehouse or forwarder. | Confirm the importer and enter its IRS/EIN number. |\n| Document amended | A value was struck through or handwritten. A container number is checked with its check digit. | Confirm with the carrier's arrival notice. |\n| Only a 6-digit HS code is given | CBP needs 10 digits. | Classify the line and enter the HTS number. |\n| Bill or invoice number differs between documents | The same number was read two ways, or the documents don't match. | Check both documents and correct the misread value. |\n| Field was hard to read | The AI model marked a value as uncertain (smudged, stamped over). | Check it against the document. |\n| Possible FDA / FCC / EPA… requirements | The goods description suggests a partner government agency may regulate them. This is a hint, not a determination. | Check the PGA flags on the 10-digit HTS number. |\n\n### 6.3 Information only the broker can supply\n\nShipping documents never carry the importer's IRS/EIN number, the bond type and surety, the filer code and entry number, the related-party declaration, or the 10-digit HTS classification. The website asks for these under **Broker inputs** and **Entry lines**.\n\n### 6.4 Defaults the website assumes\n\nEach default is stated as a finding and can be changed.\n\n| Item | Default |\n|---|---|\n| Entry type | 01 (consumption) |\n| Entry date | The estimated arrival date |\n| Port of entry | Derived from the port of discharge (for example Tacoma → 3002) |\n| Importer of record | The buyer on the invoice |\n| State of destination | The delivery address's state |\n| Entry number | Generated by NetCHB, unless you give a filer code and entry number |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Troubleshooting\n\n![File too large](manual/images/11-too-large.png)\n\n| What you see | Why | What to do |\n|---|---|---|\n| **… is over the 4.4 MB per-file limit** | The hosting platform refuses larger uploads. | Compress the scan or split it into pages. |\n| **Unsupported file type** | Only PDF and image files can be read. | Save the document as PDF, PNG or JPG. |\n| **The Gemini API key's daily quota is used up…** | The AI service's daily allowance is used up. | Try again after the reset time shown. **Use sample shipment** still works. |\n| **Gemini is overloaded right now…** | The AI service is busy. | Wait a few minutes and try again. |\n| **Reading it took longer than the server allows** | A very large or complex scan. | Try again, or upload a smaller scan. |\n| **Access code** box appears | Your administrator requires a code for reading documents. | Enter the code you were given (see below). |\n| Red **✗ XSD error** in the XML panel | Required information is missing. | Follow **What to fix…** (step 5.7). |\n| A section shows **Unable to render…** | An unusual value broke that one section; the rest still works. | Check **Extracted documents** for odd values, then click **Try again**. |\n| The document pane is blank | Some browsers, especially on phones, can't show PDFs inside a page. | Use **Open ↗** to view it in a new tab. |\n\n![Access code prompt](manual/images/12-access-code.png)\n\n**Access code.** If the website asks for one, type it in the **Access code** box and click **Extract** again. Reading documents uses a paid AI service, so administrators can protect it. The sample shipment never needs a code.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Frequently asked questions\n\n**Does the website send anything to U.S. Customs?**\nNo. It produces a file. Uploading that file to NetCHB stages the entry; a broker must transmit it from NetCHB.\n\n**Can I trust the values it changes?**\nIt changes a value only when the documents prove the correction, for example when only the recomputed amount adds up to the invoice subtotal. Each change is shown as **auto-applied** with both values, and recorded in the audit trail. Review them before filing.\n\n**Why doesn't it fill in the 10-digit HTS number?**\nClassification is a broker's legal judgement. Padding a 6-digit code would look like a real classification and could misstate duty.\n\n**What if two documents disagree?**\nThe website shows both values and the evidence for each, and never picks one silently. You decide, using the side-by-side viewer.\n\n**Does it work for shipments other than the sample?**\nYes. The rules are based on what documents mean, not on one invoice's layout. Different currencies, terms of sale, air waybills, multiple invoices, missing documents and missing data are all handled. Anything it can't settle becomes a finding.\n\n**Are my documents stored?**\nNo. Documents are read when you click **Extract** and are not kept by the website. Download the XML and the audit trail before you close the page.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Glossary\n\n| Term | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| **Assist** | Materials, tooling or design the buyer supplied free or cheaply to make the goods. Their value is added to the customs value. |\n| **CIF / FOB** | Terms of sale. A CIF price includes international freight and insurance, which are removed for customs value. An FOB price does not include them. |\n| **Entry (Type 01)** | A consumption entry: the filing that declares imported goods to U.S. Customs. |\n| **FOC / NCV** | Free of charge / no commercial value. Such goods must still be declared at a value. |\n| **House / master bill** | A forwarder's (NVOCC) bill of lading travels under the ocean carrier's master bill. Each has its own carrier code. |\n| **HTS (HTSUS)** | The 10-digit U.S. tariff classification number. Invoices often show only the first 6 digits (HS). |\n| **Importer of record (IOR)** | The party legally responsible for the entry and its duties. Often the buyer, not necessarily the bill of lading consignee. |\n| **MID** | Manufacturer identification code, built from the manufacturer's name, address and city (not from a trading company's). |\n| **NetCHB** | Customs brokerage software (Descartes NetCHB) used to file entries with U.S. Customs. |\n| **PGA** | Partner Government Agency: an agency such as FDA, FCC or EPA that regulates some goods alongside Customs. |\n| **SCAC** | The four-letter code identifying a carrier or forwarder. |\n| **XSD** | The schema that defines a valid NetCHB entry file. The website checks every file against it. |\n\n---\n\n## 10. Limits and further reading\n\n**Known limits**\n\n- 10-digit HTS classification, trade remedies (Section 301, antidumping/countervailing duties) and partner-agency filings are left to the broker.\n- With several invoices in different currencies or terms of sale, valuation uses the first invoice's; a warning says so.\n- The master bill number appears only on the bill of lading, so a misread can't be caught by comparing documents. Check it against the document.\n- On the free AI tier, the number of documents that can be read per day is limited.\n\n**Further reading**\n\n- [README](../README.md): running and deploying the website, and how it works.\n- [WRITEUP](../WRITEUP.md): the design decisions and judgement calls.\n- [schemas/SOURCE.md](../schemas/SOURCE.md): where NetCHB's format comes from.\n- [ADDING_A_RULE.md](ADDING_A_RULE.md): for developers adding a new check.\n"

# Sefer Entry Prep

Upload a shipment's documents (commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or air waybill, as PDFs or images, in any number) and get back:

1. **A NetCHB entry XML** for a CBP Type 01 consumption entry, validated in the app against NetCHB's own published `entry.xsd`.
2. **Findings**: every discrepancy between documents, every value the app changed (with both values and the reason), and every field no document can supply.

The output for the sample shipment is committed: [`output/shipment-001-entry.xml`](output/shipment-001-entry.xml) (XSD-valid) and [`output/shipment-001-findings.json`](output/shipment-001-findings.json).

- **Documents go to Google.** The website doesn't keep uploaded documents, but it sends them to Google's Gemini service to be read, and on the free tier Google's terms allow it to use that content to improve its products. The FAQ says this and recommends a paid account for client documents.

## Suggestions: what to build with more time

Each one comes from something we hit while building or testing:

1. **Independent verification of scanned identifiers.** Live tests showed the model repeatedly dropping a digit from the master bill, and a second read by the same model repeats the mistake. Make a different-model second read the default, then cross-check bill and container numbers against the carrier's arrival notice or AMS data. A wrong bill number fails cargo release.
2. **HTS classification assistant, with official agency flags.** Suggest candidate 10-digit HTSUS numbers from the description, fibre, construction and gender, citing the USITC tariff schedule and CBP CROSS rulings. The broker accepts or rejects; nothing is filled in automatically. Once classified, replace the keyword-based PGA hint with the HTS number's official PGA flags, and check Chapter 99 duties (Section 301/IEEPA).
3. **NetCHB round trip.** The WSDL discovery already found `uploadEntry` (staging only, no transmit), `queryEntryStatus`, `ManufacturerService` and `ImporterQueryService`. Wire them up behind broker credentials: stage the entry and show NetCHB's own business-rule errors, check MIDs against NetCHB's manufacturer records, and look up the importer number instead of typing it.
4. **Extraction accuracy harness in CI.** Today the eval script covers one shipment. Build a labelled set of varied documents (layouts, languages, poor scans, handwriting) and score each field per model on every change. Broker corrections from the UI then become new test cases.
5. **Persistence and a two-step workflow.** Everything currently lives in the browser tab. Add saved shipments, a preparer → licensed-broker sign-off step, roles, and a server-side, tamper-evident audit trail kept for the 5-year retention period (19 CFR 163.4).
6. **Background jobs and production model hosting.** Scans on a busy free tier took up to 3 minutes and once hit Vercel's time limit. Move extraction to a job queue with live progress, use a paid, no-data-retention model tier, and add per-user rate limits.
7. **Complete reference data and currency conversion.** Load the full CBP Schedule D (US ports) and Schedule K (foreign ports; the foreign lading port is currently left as a missing field) and full country and unit lists, kept up to date. Convert non-USD invoices with the CBP-certified rate for the export date, per invoice.
8. **More document types.** Read certificates of origin (to claim FTA / special program preferences), arrival notices and ISF data, and support informal (11) and Section 321 (86) entries.

1	# Writeup: Sefer Entry Prep
2	
3	## Approach
4	
5	I made one bet: **the model reads, the code decides.** Extraction is the only probabilistic step. It returns what each page says, verbatim, including the wrong numbers, the struck-through container and the footnotes. Reconciliation (16 rules), valuation, party resolution, MID construction and XML mapping are deterministic TypeScript with tests. That makes every number explainable and every finding reproducible. It also means `/api/entry` is a pure function, so a broker's edits rebuild the entry instantly with no model call.
6	
7	## Finding NetCHB's format
8	
9	The brief gave no link, so I went to NetCHB's own server. Its JBossWS service index exposed the `EntryUploadService` WSDL (`uploadEntry(username, password, entryXml)`). The WSDL types the entry as a bare string, so I kept probing paths until `/xml/entry/entry.xsd` answered. Its import led to `data_type.xsd`. Both are committed untouched, with hashes and the full trail, including the 404s, in `schemas/SOURCE.md`. Reading the schema turned two assumptions into facts. `<transmit/>` is what sends to CBP, so my XML omits it and only stages the entry. NetCHB computes duty unless `<precalculated/>` is set. It also exposed traps no sample would show: invoice numbers allow only `[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,17}` (so `KBAS/NB/26-0912` is invalid as printed), party names are capped at 35 characters, and origin and MID exist only per line. The sample entry validates against the real XSD, and a test proves the validator rejects broken variants.
10	
11	## Judgment calls on the sample
12	
13	| What the documents say | What I did | Why |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| Line 1 printed 6,480.00; 2,400 × 2.85 = 6,840.00 | Entered 6,840, flagged | Only 6,840 reconciles to the 21,975 subtotal, so the printed extension is the typo. Without that cross-check the rule leaves the value alone. |
16	| Both documents total 5,100 pcs | Reconciled per style: the hoodie is 1,200 vs 1,176 | The gap equals the 24 FOC samples. The invoice counts them separately, the packing list inside its total. Matching totals were camouflage. Entered at the invoice quantity, pending confirmation. |
17	| W-B220 "CMT price", buyer fabric USD 4,180 | Line value 1,260 + 4,180 = 5,440 | An assist under 19 U.S.C. 1401a(h). The XSD has no assist element, so it goes in the line value and a finding says so. |
18	| 24 FOC polo samples, "(Origin: Bangladesh)" | Kept on the entry at USD 24, origin BD, MID from SP Garments Dhaka | Free goods are still entered. The line remark overrides the invoice's single-origin declaration, which I flag as inaccurate, along with the "MADE IN VIETNAM" carton marks. |
19	| Seller in Hong Kong, factory in Binh Duong | MID `VNSAIPHO78DIA` from the factory | The MID identifies the producer. "Lot C7-C8" is ambiguous under the CFR address rule, so it is flagged for checking. |
20	| B/L consignee is a 3PL "for account of" the buyer | Importer = buyer, flagged, switchable | The consignee is a transport role. I never decide liability silently. |
21	| CIF 27,270 | Entered value 27,439 = 23,235 FOB + 4,180 assist + 24 samples | Separately stated freight 3,850 and insurance 185 are not dutiable. |
22	| Container 1728 struck through, 1722 handwritten | Used 1722, error-level finding | The ISO 6346 check digit says 1728 cannot exist. It still needs the carrier's arrival notice to confirm. |
23	| HS 6-digit only | Emitted as printed, never zero-padded | A padded code looks like a real classification. The schema accepts 5 to 10 digits, so the file stays valid while NetCHB flags it. |
24	
25	Also caught: gross weight 1,888 vs 1,930 kg (the packing list says "palletized: NO", so pallets don't explain it), hoodie fibre 60/40 cotton vs "TC 65/35" (which flips the chief fibre and therefore the HTS subheading), and the ambiguous date 12/09/2026, resolved to 12 Sep because only that reading precedes shipment.
26	
27	## What I don't know
28	
29	- 10-digit HTS classification is broker judgment, and so are Chapter 99 remedies.
30	- The bill-number format (whether to strip the SCAC prefix) is inferred from AMS convention, not stated by NetCHB.
31	- Whether NetCHB's business rules accept everything the XSD accepts: I had no account to test an upload.
32	- Which container number is real, until the carrier confirms.
33	
34	## Generalising
35	
36	Rules are written against document meaning, never this invoice's layout. Seven synthetic variants run in the test suite: EUR on FOB terms, CIF without itemised freight, an air waybill, invoice only, no HS codes, seller-is-factory, and two invoices. Each degrades honestly, with no crashes and findings that say what's missing. Building the variants found two real gaps, which I fixed: seller-as-manufacturer, and multi-invoice handling (now warned about).
37	
38	Running real extraction (Gemini) on the three sample PDFs scored 97–98% field accuracy against the hand-written fixture, and every trap was still caught from the model's own output. The live runs also exposed three bugs the clean fixture never could:
39	- A sister factory in Bangladesh was being borrowed as the MID source for the Vietnam lines.
40	- A "supplied free of charge by buyer" assist note made a line look free, which cancelled the 6,840 correction.
41	- A generic "contracted factory" description was being treated as a manufacturer.
42	
43	Each is fixed, and pinned by a test built from the real output. The model's answers also vary between runs, which is exactly why the deterministic layer guards against plausible extraction shapes rather than trusting one.
44	
45	## Built for how a broker actually works
46	
47	A broker's job is verification, and their liability is the record. So the review screen keeps the source document beside the data. Every piece of quoted evidence links back to the page it came from, so checking an extracted value takes one click, not a hunt through a PDF viewer.
48	
49	Customs is not only tariffs. A line can also need FDA, FCC, EPA or other agency data. CBP decides that from the 10-digit HTS number, which these documents don't carry. So the app gives an early warning from the goods description. It names the agency, the word that triggered it, and the `entry.xsd` block where the data is filed or disclaimed. It is explicit that this is a hint, not a determination. On the sample it stays silent, which is right for adult apparel. I tuned it against apparel false positives ("ivory" is a colour, faux fur is not wildlife).
50	
51	Brokers must keep entry records for five years (19 CFR 163.4), and when CBP asks why an entry was filed a certain way, the answer has to be on paper. The audit export records:
52	- what the model read, and every manual edit as an exact before/after;
53	- each correction the rules made, with its evidence, kept separate from the issues still open;
54	- the final XML;
55	- hashes tying the record to the specific source files and schema.
56	
57	Building it surfaced a real provenance bug: git's Windows line-ending conversion had silently rewritten the "byte-for-byte" schema copy. A `.gitattributes` now pins those bytes, and a test checks the schema hash on every run.
58	
59	Finally, each panel has its own error boundary, so an odd document that breaks one view degrades that panel, not the whole screen.
60	
61	## Testing the live deployment
62	
63	I tested the deployed app the way a grader would: the sample, twelve shipment variants (with live results byte-identical to local), a single combined PDF, a phone photo, junk files, and oversized uploads. That surfaced issues no unit test had:
64	- Two correct invoices were reported as arithmetic *errors*, because every line was checked against the first invoice's totals. Now each invoice is reconciled and entered on its own.
65	- A 5 MB scan produced a cryptic JSON parse error. Now uploads go one file per request, and oversized files are refused up front with the reason.
66	- The free Gemini tier allows 20 requests per model per day, and it ran out mid-test. Quota exhaustion is now recognised, skipped past model by model, and explained to the broker.
67	
68	One idea failed when tested, and I kept the lesson. To catch misread bill numbers I added a second, focused read of the identifiers. Live, both reads dropped the *same* digit from the master bill. Two reads by one model are not independent, and the check doubled quota use. So it is now opt-in with a *different* model. The free default is a deterministic check instead: numbers printed on two documents (the B/L number on the invoice, invoice numbers on the B/L) must agree.
69	
70	## With more time
71	
72	One `<invoice>` per source invoice. An HTS assistant backed by CROSS rulings. Schedule D/K tables loaded from CBP. NetCHB `ManufacturerService` lookup for MIDs. A real `uploadEntry` call behind broker credentials. Broker corrections fed back as extraction examples.
73	
74	## Using AI
75	
76	I used AI assistants throughout: recon, reading the 6,700-line XSD, scaffolding, rules and tests. The full chat history is in the submission. The fixture the tests check against was hand-transcribed, not model-generated, so the model never grades its own work.
